PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: Allo Towers is requesting FAA approval to construct a 120' guyed radio tower with a top mounted 5' lightning rod for a total structure height of 125' AGL. This radio tower will be leveraged by the State of North Dakota for their Statewide Interoperable Radio Network (SIRN) that provides mission critical radio coverage to local and state public safety and public service end users. The state has not yet determined the specific radio channels and frequencies to be allocated to this radio site. This site is currently named as Echo  and will likely be renamed to Jamestown. The SIRN system will leverage the several 12.5 kHz bandwidth channels out of the public safety 769-775 MHz and/or 851-869 MHz band. Maximum Effected Radiated Power in these bands is 100w/.1kw. nThis future ND SIRN tower site will be initially installed with three (3) RFI CC807-11T1 antennas  one (1) TXRX 428E TTA  three (3) 7/8" coax  one (1) 1/2" coax  five (5) foot lightning rod.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: This site is located in Stutsman County  ND. The new tower will be constructed in pasture land. The site is located on the attached portion of the associated USGS 7 1/2 minute Quadrangle map.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The project consists of Hayhoe Trail (Holt-Mason Trail) from College Road (POB) to Kerns Road (POE). The total project length is 1.70 miles. The project includes constructing an HMA shared-use path with a pedestrian bridge  drainage improvements  tree removals  clearing  permanent signing  and permanent pavement markings. The proposed cross section typically consists of a 10 foot HMA shared-use path with 2 foot clear width on both sides. The shared-use path will be 2 inches thick with 6 inches of aggregate base. Path slopes will tie into the existing ground. A pedestrian bridge will also be constructed over US-127 south of the existing overpass bridge. Drainage improvements will be included to facilitate positive drainage where necessary. The project will require tree removals and clearing for the construction of the shared-use path. Disturbed areas will be restored by seeding and mulching. Easements and consent to grades will be required for the construction of the shared-use path. Please see the attached documents for exact locations of easements  grading permits  clearing  and tree removals.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The project area consists of 7 Mile Road from Erickson Road (POB) to Pinconning Road (POE). The total project length is 3.92 miles. The project includes HMA base crushing and shaping (estimated 7 inch depth)  HMA resurfacing  shoulder improvements  drainage improvements  slope restoration  and permanent pavement markings. The existing road typically consists of 11 foot lanes and 5 foot gravel shoulders. The proposed section consists of 11 foot lanes  3 foot paved shoulders  and 1 foot gravel shoulders. Roadway slopes will tie into the existing ground. Drainage improvements will be included to facilitate positive drainage. The existing box culvert at Johnson Drain will be retained but will include removal and repair of the headwalls. Two existing cross culverts under the road will be removed and replaced; all other cross culverts will be retained but will include removing the headwalls and extending the culvert ends. The existing storm sewer will be retained and extended as needed. Additionally  the guardrail at the Pinconning River bridge will be removed and replaced. All roadwork will be contained within the existing road ROW. There will not be a need for ROW acquisition. Any disturbed areas will be restored by seeding and mulching. The ground disturbing activities on this project include HMA base crushing and shaping  slope restoration  and new guardrail posts from the POB to the POE.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The proposed solar photovoltaic (PV) ground-mounted  east-west tracking array  structure is planned for construction to be located on the Red Lake Nation reservation  home of the Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians. The Red Lake DNR site is located near the intersection of West Bot Drive and Thunderlake Drive  in the Red Lake municipality area  in Minnesota  as shown in the site map included with this notice. The east-west azimuth tracking solar array will follow the location of the sun from east to west during the daylight hours. The planned size of the solar array is approximately 3.48 MW (DC)  which would use approximately six-thousand (6 000)  or possibly more  solar panels located outside of a 200 foot radius from the existing Red Lake DNR helicopter landing pad. The height of the proposed solar array is not expected to exceed 15 feet AGL. There are existing mature trees within the 200' landing pad radius  which are much taller than 15 fee AGL and existing one-story buildings outside the helicopter landing pad 200 foot radius as close as 380 feet from the landing pad. The proposed solar tracking array would be located between Red Lake Elementary School and the Red Lake DNR helicopter landing pad site and not taller than any of the school buildings. The proposed solar array will be less than the height of existing mature trees and buildings located at the site. Red Lake Nation DNR has requested that we file this notice for FAA approval.
